# Mission — Make Search Discovery a Real Public Door

The Awtsmoos reveals no doorway through an imagined URL; Awtsmoos.com must answer in public truth, with crawlable Torah flowing from root to route.

## User-visible mission

Turn the current local SEO work into a real production capability on canonical `main`:

- `https://awtsmoos.com/sitemap.xml` must return real XML, not 404.
- `https://awtsmoos.com/robots.txt` must return real crawler guidance.
- `/heichelos/sitemap.xml` must be a fast useful seed map, not an expensive recursive computation.
- Heichel and series HTML must expose ordinary crawlable links.
- numeric Road routes must server-render the real Torah teaching before JavaScript.
- canonical named-post URLs must remain stable and indexable.
- nonexistent posts must remain non-indexable.

## Broad possibilities considered

1. Static root sitemap plus dynamic Heichel sitemap.
2. One giant recursive dynamic sitemap.
3. Per-Heichel recursive sitemaps.
4. Generated sitemap artifacts during deploy.
5. Search-index-driven sitemap generation.
6. Fast seed sitemap plus semantic HTML graph traversal.
7. Root dynamic routing for robots/sitemap.

The rejected deep-recursion designs already proved capable of 30–120 second timeouts and server monopolization. The strongest practical architecture is a real static root sitemap plus a fast privacy-filtered Heichel seed sitemap, while server-rendered HTML links reveal deeper series and named posts.

## Release reality

The local branch is `main`. Local committed HEAD is ahead of freshly fetched `origin/main`. SEO changes remain modified/untracked in the shared working tree. Production currently returns 404 for `/sitemap.xml`, proving the local work was never activated publicly.
